<thought>We need a neutral molecule whose formula matches the mass spectrum (C₉H₈ClO₂ or close). Adding one carbon to the phenylacetic acid gives phenylpropionic acid with a chlorine substituent: SMILES “Clc1ccc(cc1)CCC(=O)O”. This structure has formula C₉H₉ClO₂, which is consistent with the observed m/z 183 (likely the deprotonated anion in negative‑mode ESI). The SMILES is valid and represents a plausible candidate.</thought>
<final_answer>Clc1ccc(cc1)CCC(=O)O</final_answer>
